title: ci(gate): every imported package must be declared by the package that ships it (#4394)
body:
Fixes #4394

## The trap being closed

A bare specifier *resolving* from a package directory says nothing about whether that package *declares* it. The workspace root carries `devDependencies.react`, so a `node_modules/react` symlink sits at the root and Node's — and TypeScript's — upward directory walk reaches it from **any** package directory. The card's own probe, re-run on this branch's tree:

```
require.resolve('react', { paths: ['packages/core/src'] })
  -> /home/user/objectui-4394/node_modules/.pnpm/react@19.2.8/node_modules/react/index.js
@object-ui/core declares 'react' in: (NO FIELD AT ALL)
```

pnpm's isolated `node_modules` prevents phantom dependencies *between workspace packages*; it does not defend a package against the root's own dev dependencies. So a dependency-direction check performed **by resolution** — the obvious way to "measure the actual import graph", which is what #4389's brief asked for — returns the wrong answer, confidently, and the disagreement stays silent until somebody else's install.

`pnpm check:phantom-deps` asks the other question, the one root hoisting cannot answer for anyone: **is it declared**.

## Violation-surface reading, and the landing it picked

Measured first, over `src/**` of all 40 packages in the changeset `fixed` group — 2641 files, 12664 module specifiers. The full reading, by tier:

| tier | checked | undeclared on `main` |
|---|---|---|
| runtime files (ship) | 3539 package imports | **7 sites / 2 distinct pairs** |
| tooling files (test, bench) | 3693 package imports | 1873 sites / 76 pairs, of which 74 pairs are 4 root-installed tool names |
| node builtins | 175 | 0 in a runtime file of a package without `@types/node` |
| self-references | 4 | 0 (all in `__benchmarks__`, and core declares `exports`) |

**Landing: enforcing, no baseline ledger.** The runtime surface was a small fixable set, and both entries are resolved in this PR rather than baselined:

1. **`@object-ui/plugin-detail` -> `react-router-dom`, 2 sites — a real defect, fixed.** `PermissionFacetLink.tsx:10` and `record-reference-rail.tsx:22` take `Link` and `useParams` from the router; the manifest named it in no field at all, while all three siblings using the same hooks (`app-shell`, `layout`, `plugin-designer`) declare it as a peer of `^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0`. Not latent: that package's rollup config externalises every bare specifier (`external: (id) => !/^[./]/.test(id) && !id.startsWith(__dirname)`), so the published `dist/index.js` carried an import the manifest never mentioned. Fixed with the siblings' range — a fourth spelling of the same claim is the #3741 mistake — plus a `patch` changeset, since a published manifest gaining a peer is user-visible.
2. **`object-ui` (the VS Code extension) -> `vscode`, 5 sites — graded, not fixed.** The extension host injects it; it is not a runtime npm package and declaring it as a dependency would produce an uninstallable package. Handled as a `HOST_PROVIDED` entry that the package **earns** by declaring `@types/vscode` and `engines.vscode`, both re-checked on every run.

The tooling tier's 1873 is not baselined either, and the reason is in the shape of the number: 74 of its 76 pairs are exactly `vitest`, `@testing-library/react`, `@testing-library/jest-dom`, `@testing-library/user-event` — one coherent convention, this repo installing its test toolchain once at the root. Demanding thirty packages re-declare those is churn that protects no consumer, because nothing published resolves those files. So a tooling file may be answered by the package's own fields **or the workspace root's**, and the size of that concession is printed on every run (`1878 tooling import(s) are declared only by the workspace root`) rather than absorbed. What it still catches is the real thing: a test import of a package declared *nowhere*.

## Pre-fix RED (#4118)

Two directions, both captured. **First, the card's exact synthetic case** — a throwaway `packages/core/src/__phantom_probe_4394__.ts` containing `import { useState } from 'react'` plus `import type { ReactNode } from 'react'`, created and deleted without touching any existing file, and not present in this branch:

```
## 3. TypeScript is GREEN on it - resolution, not declaration, is what tsc asks
   diagnostics on the probe file: 0 (no TS2307 "Cannot find module" - it resolved)

## 4. The gate is RED on the same tree
      packages/core/src/__phantom_probe_4394__.ts:4:1  [undeclared-runtime]  @object-ui/core imports 'react' -> react
      packages/core/src/__phantom_probe_4394__.ts:5:1  [undeclared-runtime]  @object-ui/core imports 'react' -> react (type-only)
   (exit 1)
```

That is the false-GREEN in one frame: `tsc` reports **zero** diagnostics — not `TS2307` — because it asked whether the module resolves, and it does.

**Second, and stronger, the gate was red on unmodified `main`** — this class was already live, so the pre-fix red needed no synthesis:

```
❌  2 import(s) are not declared where a consumer would find them (1 distinct package/dependency pair(s)):
      packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/PermissionFacetLink.tsx:10:1  [undeclared-runtime]  ...
      packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-reference-rail.tsx:22:1  [undeclared-runtime]  ...
```

## Reverse verification

Predicted direction first, then run:

- **Delete the gate script -> the self-test cannot pass vacuously.** Predicted red at the *import*, not at an assertion; measured `Cannot find module '../check-phantom-dependencies.mjs'`, `0 test`, exit 1. Restored.
- **Take the `plugin-detail` fix back out (`git checkout origin/main -- packages/plugin-detail/package.json`) -> gate exit 1, and exactly two self-tests red** (`has no phantom dependency`, `pins the defect this gate found`), 40 of 42 still passing. Restored.
- **One bug this found in its own first run, now pinned as a regression.** `node:fs` is not a legal package name — npm allows no `:` — so asking the package-name grammar *before* the builtin check filed all 127 `node:`-prefixed imports as path aliases and graded none of them. **The verdict did not move; only a counter did** (`alias=127, builtin=48` instead of `alias=0, builtin=175`), which is why the self-test pins it by counter.

## The gradings, each stated rather than buried

- **Type-only imports are STRICT** — judged exactly like a value import. The emitted `.d.ts` keeps the reference, so a consumer type-checking against the package needs those types installed; it is one edit from becoming a value import with nothing reporting the promotion; and a carve-out here is the tolerant-consumer shape AGENTS.md #0.1 rejects. Measured cost today: **zero** — none of the 7 runtime violations was type-only, so strictness is free at the moment it lands.
- **Node builtins need `@types/node`** in any of the package's own fields, `devDependencies` included — a types package is never a runtime import, so `dependencies` would be the wrong field. Measured: every builtin import in a package lacking it is in a tooling file (33 pairs, all of them); every runtime builtin import (`@object-ui/cli`'s `fs`/`path`/`url`/`child_process`) is in a package that declares it.
- **`@/…` is skipped by GRAMMAR, not by an alias list** — npm has no empty scope, so it cannot name a package.
- **`@object-ui/console` is the one exemption**, and it is re-derived every run: an application build (`vite build`, no `build.lib`, no `rollupOptions.external`) inlines its ~325 devDependency imports into the `dist/` bundle it publishes. If either property changes the exemption fails loudly instead of quietly covering a package that has started shipping bare imports.

## Stated scope

`src/**` of the changeset `fixed` group, read from `.changeset/config.json` for the reason `check-changeset-presence.mjs` gives — a hand-written glob misses `apps/console`. **Not** checked: the reverse direction (a declared dependency nothing imports), files outside `src/`, and **layering** — "may `@object-ui/core` import React at all" is AGENTS.md §3 and #4389, and a core *test* importing React satisfies this gate while still being wrong. Answering a second question badly is worse than not answering it.

One honesty correction made during review: an earlier draft of the header claimed every build program excludes tests or emits nothing from them. #4006 has **measured** the opposite (73 `*.test.d.ts` in published `dist/`), and three packages list `src` in `files`. The claim that actually holds — and the one the tooling tier rests on — is that nothing *resolves* those files, so no install can fail on them. Header corrected to say that and to point at #4006; measurement added as a [comment there](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/4006#issuecomment-5261846024) rather than as a twin issue.

## Verification

- `node scripts/check-phantom-dependencies.mjs` — green on the merged tree (40 packages, 2648 files, 12700 specifiers).
- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/` — **39 files, 893 tests passed**, including the new 42-test self-test and `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts`, which pins the doc job-table row against `ci.yml` in both directions.
- `pnpm type-check:scripts` — clean (`BundledApplication` typedef added so the injectable exemption table types through `allowJs`).
- `pnpm exec eslint` on both new files — clean. `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` — OK; plus a `grep -naP` self-scan of every touched file for control bytes beyond the gate's surface (none).
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` / `check-changeset-fixed.mjs` / `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` — green.
- **YAML re-parse proof** for the `ci.yml` edit: parses; the new step sits at index 7 of the `type-check` job, immediately after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` at index 6, carrying the same `if: steps.relevant.outputs.should_run == 'true'` guard as its siblings.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` — clean, so the 3-line lockfile change is in sync.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/PermissionFacetLink.sduiCarrier.test.tsx` — 2 passed (the renderer whose import was undeclared).

## Risks

- The lockfile gains 3 lines. `.gitattributes` routes `pnpm-lock.yaml` through the `pnpm-merge` driver, so a concurrent branch conflicts textually rather than silently.
- The gate is the first thing to run after install in `type-check`, so a phantom import now fails the job **before** the slower gates — intended, but it changes which red a contributor sees first.
